# Review — cid-tiradas-35-39 (tiradas 35–39, lines 715–777 incl. 734b, 755b)

Adversarial review against the pinned packet, Pidal's rubrics and footnotes on the scan (PDF pp. 176–181, read on
the image, with crops at 500 dpi for 730–735 and the italics), Pidal's introduction pp. 19–21 and 97 (PDF 23–25,
101; text layer only to confirm what his footnotes point to), conventions.md, the pilot (01-04), 19-23 and the
preceding part (32-34). All edits made by script (json load/dump, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1). No `t` changed:
the 65 `t` lines concatenated equal the packet's 65 lines exactly (checked by script after the edits); one `l`
line per `t` line in all 25 units.

Checked and found sound (no change):
- Rubrics against the scan: 35 Los del Cid acometen para socorrer a Pedro Vermúdez; 36 Destrozan las haces
  enemigas; 37 Mención de los principales caballeros cristianos; 38 Minaya en peligro. — El Cid hiere a Fáriz;
  39 Galve herido y los moros derrotados. The assonances are right: 35 ó-e with bare-ó lines (paragogic -e, as the
  pilot's tirada 3); 36 á with sangre, Yagüe in á-e; 37 ó with Salvadórez; 38 á-o throughout; 39 á with Galve,
  aparte, carne in á-e.
- Pidal's footnotes are reported correctly: 713 (falssar, cites 728), 715, 721 (custom, Don Juan Manuel's quotation, the cry repeated at 1140),
  724 (sendos), 725 (carga de tornada, "v. p. 97": checked, p. 97 is the introduction, the charge en retour),
  728 (desmallar), 731 (Bismi Allahi; Archbishop Rodrigo, Clavijo, "Dios ayuda y Santiago"), 735/737/738 (each
  only a pointer to the introduction, pp. 19, 21, 20, plus "criado por el Cid, comp. v. 2902": the drafter's claim
  holds), 747, 749 (al-wazir), 751 (Búcar, swords, Godfrey of Bouillon), 754 (bando), 755 (firmes están, no se
  van), 758 (delibrar; Alexandre 488), 764 (rancar; 793, 814, 1656, 1819), 766, 771 (2079, 3139, 1965), 772 (alcaz,
  alcança, alcanço), 777 (segudar).
- Flags: 734b: on the image the label 730 sits beside "tantos pendones blancos" (the 729 line), and Pidal's
  footnotes put 728 on desmanchar and 731 on Mafómat, so the six lines from cavallos to "mio Çid Ruy Diaz" have only
  730–734 available. The note states this and says the letter b is ours. Which of the two lines takes the b
  cannot be decided from the print; putting it on the second line of the exclamation is a reasonable choice. 755b:
  wholly italic on the image ("a menester que los cometamos de cabo"), unnumbered, flagged in the note as
  Pidal's restoration and the letter as ours.
- Italics/brackets checked on the image: abu[el]tas, na[çió], de[l Criador], R[o]y ×3, Vermu[doz], [muertos],
  falssa[r e], Ca[d]ien, [por el campo], f[o] ×2, Albar[oz], Garcia[z], buen[a], destella[n]do, [e della],
  Ter[rer], Cataluyu[t]h, Calatayu[t]h. "Ruy Diaz" (734b) in roman without an accent and "Martin" (738)
  without an accent are confirmed on the 500-dpi crop. The note does not hide either. In `l`, restored words and name
  endings keep their brackets (Vermu[doz], Ter[rer] as in 32-34), and single restored letters inside ordinary words
  are dropped (There-were-falling, was, good, dripping).
- Grammar labels: enbraçan, ívanlos, feridlos, so, seños, veriedes, ca[d]ien (imperfect -ié), a quebrada
  (participle agreement), acostós, diol, cortól, sodes, abré, firme', nos', a menester, cometamos (pres. subj.),
  fuerte mientre, valos delibrando, nasco, avié dado, fallen (present of fallir), únol, írsele, rancado,
  echógelas (ge = le), gel, Arrancado es (singular with double subject), firiendo (absolute gerund), se fo entrar,
  nol: all right.
- House renderings: "born in a good hour" (719, 759); "my Çid", "Çid" in `i`; Minaya Álvar Fáñez in `i`, Álbar in
  `l`; Ruy Díaz of Vivar; Per Vermudoz; Terrer, Calatayud as in 24-34; Álvar Álvarez, Álvar Salvadórez as in 19-23.
- Nothing bowdlerized. Uncertain points are marked as uncertain: the referent of gel's lo, que llegó (blow or cut),
  the subject of cogieron (now hedged), the 734b numbering.

Findings refused:
- `i` 761 "the third has caught him" for el únol ha tomado ('the one'): after "los dos" the remaining blow is the
  third; this is idiomatic English and the note gives the literal sense. Left.
- Note 723 "Pidal glosses seños moros 'uno cada uno'": he writes the modern 'sendos moros' with that gloss in
  brackets. The substance is the same. Left.
- Note 754 a menester "there is need" (impersonal) beside `l` "it-has need": these agree. Whether the subject is
  impersonal or the Çid makes no difference to the sense. Left.
- Note 726 premer 'couched for the thrust' / alçar 'to strike again': this interprets the line and is not attributed
  to Pidal. It is plausible. Left.

Checked: the gloss keys (95, excluding __broaden__) equal the novel-forms.json keys exactly. Every
__broaden__ value (13) begins with the known-forms.json entry exactly, then " · " (checked by script). The broadens
are justified by the text: de (de pie, de suso de, de cabo, de fuertes coraçones), a (a quebrada with
agreement), mandó 'held', mayor (place name), passar 'pierce', firme' (plural, s lost), nos' (= non se), cabo (de
cabo), avié (auxiliary), dado (participle), castellano (epithet of the Çid), diestro (adjective), medio 'half'.
No broaden is missing: the existing entries already cover y 'and/there', so 'I am/his', fo 'went' (se fo entrar),
es (passive), part 'side', quanto 'as fast as', aun 'yet', al espada, lanças 'horsemen', ya 'already'. The other
entries were checked against the text and found right in lemma, person, number, tense and mood: ívanlos,
fieren, matáronle (dative of the person affected), quebrada, víolo, acostós, tenié, diol, cortól, ival, abré,
cometamos (pres. subj.), valos, fallen (fallir, not hallar), írsele, rancado, echógelas (ge = le), gel (hedged),
arrancado, fuyen, firiendo, cogieron, alcaz, duró. Proper names are hedged where uncertain: Muño/Nuño "probably
related", Félez < Felix "probably". Fáriz and Galve are already in the glossary marked "fictional, says Pidal".

Findings refused:
- della "de + ella … from all sides": whether ella is the pronoun or an old demonstrative here is not something
  the reader needs. The gloss gives Pidal's sense ('de una y de otra parte'). Left.
- exorado "probably so": an unnecessary hedge on Latin exauratus, but it does no harm. Left.
- abaxan "modern abajar survives only as a rare, dialectal word": loosely put, but not wrong. Left.
- cogieron 'took in, received' (= acogieron): this agrees with the units reading, which is now hedged in the note.
  The gloss gives the sense of the form. Left.
